items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And sold it, I sold it to Achey.

ctx.x: When did you take up the bass do you remember about, was it time of the war or?

Around just about, just about the time of the war. Around 1917, yeah, around, no, around 1912. Before the war. Yeah, before the war I'd take no bass. And from then on I'd play bass, right on. Now and then I'd play, you know, if I catch a job you see, I'd play banjo in between you see, because I never did play study with, you know I'd play study with a band one time and then another fella hired me you know like that. My band wouldn't have enough work all the time to keep me busy. Somebody always wanted a hymn in a…

I had a good one too. I let him have it. I got tired of being bothered with it, you know. And practically most when I was using it, they would always come from me for congo day to play on them trucks, you know. And I got tired of going on them jobs on it. The weather got so bad and I'd be sitting up on them trucks playing that banjo, I just got tired of doing that and I just put it down. I said I'll get rid of the banjo when the fellas want to hire me. They couldn't get me.
